findings.claim: The paper's RAECSDC polarization condition and its multiplier formula disagree; the item copies both, so its statement is false. The paper writes π^∨ ≅ π^c ⊗ (χ∘N_{F/F+}∘det) and claims multiplier ν∘r_{π,ι} = ε^{1−n} r_{χ,ι}. The cited source fixes the convention the other way round. BLGGT §2.1 defines a polarized pair by π^c ≅ π^∨ ⊗ (χ∘N_{F/F+}∘det), and BLGGT Theorem 2.1.1(1) gives multiplier ε^{1−n} r(χ), where 'polarized' means r^c ≅ r^∨ ⊗ μ. Under the paper's displayed convention the BLGGT character is χ^{−1}, so the multiplier is ε^{1−n} r_{χ,ι}^{−1}. Check at n = 1: π = ψ is an algebraic Hecke character of a CM field. The display gives ψψ^c = (χ∘N)^{−1}, so μ|_{G_F} = r_ψ r_ψ^c = r_{χ,ι}^{−1}|_{G_F}, not r_{χ,ι}. Take ψ of infinity type z ↦ z^{−1} over an imaginary quadratic field, with χ adjusted by δ_{F/Q} so that χ_v(−1) = −1. Then r_χ² ≠ 1, and the item's formula is false. The paper applies the multiplier only with χ quadratic up to norm, for example ν∘s = ε^{1−n}δ^n on p. 13. Inversion is invisible there, so no result of the paper changes; only the recalled statement, and the item that copies it, are wrong.

findings.claim: The item defines the base level as 'U₀ = ∏ U_{0,v} (Iwahori at Σ, maximal elsewhere)'. That is not the paper's definition. At v ∈ Σ the quaternion algebra D is ramified and the paper takes the whole unit group, U_{0,v} = (D ⊗_F F_v)^×. Some proofs depend on this choice. The proof of Proposition 4.4 uses it to force π_{1,v} to be exactly Steinberg rather than a twist of Steinberg. With the maximal compact O_{D_v}^× (the only sensible reading of 'Iwahori' in a division algebra), forms of the unramified quadratic twist of Steinberg also occur. For p odd, localising at m_D removes them, since r̄|G_{F_v} is trivial and the twist reduces to −1 at Frob_v. For p = 2 they survive. Their Galois representations are extensions of χε^{−1} by χ with χ ≠ 1 unramified, which are not of type R_v. So Proposition 4.4(3), the R_Q-module structure, fails, and the dyadic argument loses its local condition at Σ. The item also omits the local conditions at p that m_D imposes: T_v^{(1)} ∈ m_D (non-ordinary), T_v^{(1)} − 1 ∈ m_D (ordinary), and T_v^{(2)} − 1 ∈ m_D for v ∈ S_p − Σ_p. These conditions select the local types on the quaternionic side.

findings.claim: The item omits the standing hypothesis of the cited lemma, and as written the statement is false. The item reads 'A subgroup of GL_n(O) is enormous if the derived subgroup of the identity component of its Zariski closure acts absolutely irreducibly and contains regular semisimple elements.' [NT23, Lemma 2.28] assumes that the characteristic polynomial of every h ∈ H has all its roots in E. Definition 2.23 needs an h with n distinct eigenvalues in E, so the hypothesis cannot be dropped. Counterexample: take E = Q_p with p odd, an anisotropic ternary quadratic form q over E, and H = SO(q)(E), which is compact and preserves a lattice. H is Zariski dense in SO(q). Over Ē, SO(q) is PGL₂ acting by the adjoint representation, which is absolutely irreducible, semisimple, and contains regular semisimple elements. But an h ∈ H with an eigenvalue t ∈ E, t ≠ ±1, would have an E-rational isotropic eigenvector (q(v) = t²q(v)), which is impossible. So no element of H has three distinct eigenvalues in E, and H is not enormous.
findings.evidence: NT23 (arXiv 1912.11265v3 TeX, read 1 Oct 2026), Definition 2.23: 'We say that a subgroup H ⊂ GL_n(O) is enormous if for all simple E[H]-submodules V ⊂ W_E, we can find h ∈ H with n distinct eigenvalues in E and α ∈ E such that α is an eigenvalue of h and tr e_{h,α}V ≠ 0.' Lemma 2.28: 'Suppose that for each h ∈ H, the characteristic polynomial of h has all of its roots in E. … (2) Let G ⊂ GL_n denote the Zariski closure of H. If G° contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly on E^n, then H is enormous.' (The numbering 2.23 and 2.28 was checked by counting the shared theorem counter in §2.)

Proposition 4.8 needs, for every N, a set Q of q primes with q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, split in K, killing H¹(F_S/F, ad⁰ r̄(1)), and with (r̄ ⊗ s̄)(Frob_ṽ) having 2r distinct eigenvalues. The paper discusses adapting the Taylor–Wiles lemma only for p = 2 (citing hypothesis (6)). For p > 2 it says the proof is 'essentially identical' to [NT21b, Proposition 2.6], changing only the unitary level structure. But the p ≠ 2 lemma of NT21b (Lemma 2.7) keeps its regularity condition by replacing σ with τσ for τ ∈ G_{L(ζ_{p^N})}, where L is the field cut out by Proj r̄. That works for Sym^{n−1} r̄, which depends only on Proj r̄(σ) up to a scalar. It does not control s̄(τσ), so (r̄ ⊗ s̄)(τσ) need not stay regular. The adaptation is to take τ in the kernel of r̄ and s̄ modulo scalars, with M the field cut out by r̄, s̄, K and ζ_{p^N}. This works whenever φ|G_M ≠ 0. Otherwise it needs Hom_Γ(Gal(M/LK(ζ_{p^N}))^{ab}, ad⁰ r̄(1)) = 0. findings.claim: The p > 2 component argument rests on 'R_loc = ⊗̂ R_v is an O-flat domain of dimension 1 + 3[F:Q] + 3|S|'. The paper gives no reference, and no item records the input. A completed tensor product over O of complete local O-flat domains need not be a domain. For example, A = O[√ϖ] = O⟦x⟧/(x² − ϖ) is a domain with residue field k, but A ⊗̂_O A = O[x,y]/(x²−ϖ, y²−ϖ) has (x−y)(x+y) = 0. So the step needs geometric integrality of each R_v: R_v ⊗_O O′ is a domain for every finite O′/O, or equivalently its irreducible components are geometrically irreducible. It also needs the dimension formula dim ⊗̂R_v = 1 + Σ(dim R_v − 1). kisin-local-rings and local-quotients-4 state only 'domain'. kisin-local-rings even drops 'domain' for the Σ^p and S_∞ rings, and drops the dimension 4 + [F_v:Q_p] for Snowden's ring.

findings.claim: New gap. The proof of Lemma 3.3 normalises the image h of complex conjugation to diag(1,−1) by GL₂(F_{p^a})-conjugation. This is impossible whenever h is a non-split involution of PGL₂(F_q), q = p^a. That is forced when the projective image is PSL₂(F_q) with q ≡ 3 mod 4, a case the §3 set-up explicitly allows. An involution of PGL₂(F_q) is represented by a trace-zero A with A² = μ ≠ 0. It is split, that is GL₂(F_q)-conjugate to diag(1,−1), iff μ is a square, and it lies in PSL₂(F_q) iff det A = −μ is a square. For q ≡ 3 mod 4 the two conditions exclude each other. Since PSL₂(F_q) is normal, no conjugate of h ∈ PSL₂(F_q) is diag(1,−1). Example: r̄(c) = i·A with A ∈ SL₂(F_q), A² = −1 and i ∉ F_q, which has det −1 = ε^{−1}(c). The lemma itself is still true. E16's repairs ('take α a generator of F_{p^a}^×') inherit the same split normalisation.
findings.evidence: Proof of Lemma 3.3, arXiv v2 pp. 15–16: 'The image of the homomorphism Proj r̄_{π,ι} × ε : G_F → PGL₂(F_{p^a}) × F_p^× contains PSL₂(F_{p^a}) × {1} and an element of the form (h, −1) (image of complex conjugation), where h² = 1, h ≠ 1. Conjugating r̄_{π,ι} by an element of GL₂(F_{p^a}), we can assume that h = diag(1, −1) mod centre. … We consider elements of the form g = diag(α, α^{−1}) mod centre, α ∈ F_{p^a}^×.' §3 opening, p. 13: 'the image of Proj r̄_{π,ι} is equal either to PSL₂(F_{p^a}) or PGL₂(F_{p^a})'. a = 5, p = 7 gives q ≡ 3 mod 4.
findings.fix: Record a new sourceIssue (kind gap; affects nothing; locator: proof of Lemma 3.3, arXiv v2 pp. 15–16). Correction: let C be the maximal torus of PGL₂ over F_q through h. C is split if h is split and non-split otherwise. C(F_q) is cyclic of order q ∓ 1, and the eigenvalue ratio identifies it with μ_{q∓1}. For g ∈ C(F_q) ∩ PSL₂(F_q) (index 2), the ratios of gh form −H with H = μ_{(q∓1)/2}. If |H| is even, take x a generator: then x^i = −1 forces i ≡ |H|/2 mod |H|, and |H|/2 ≥ (q−1)/4 > r. If |H| is odd, take x = −ρ with ρ a generator: then (−ρ)^i = −1 forces i odd and ρ^i = 1, so i ≥ |H| > r. Either way x^i ≠ q_v^{±1} = −1 for 0 ≤ i ≤ r, and Chebotarev applies to (gh, −1). Amend E16's correction so that it refers to this torus rather than to diag(α, α^{−1}).

findings.claim: The paper has a gap in Lemma 5.7(2) that the extraction did not record. It deduces irreducibility of the tensor product from irreducibility of each factor over G_L, L = M_π ∩ M_σ. That inference fails in general, since the tensor product of two irreducible representations of a group can be reducible. What makes it work is that M_π and M_σ are linearly disjoint over L, so G_L surjects onto Gal(M_π/L) × Gal(M_σ/L) ⊇ PSL₂ × PSL₂. Then Std ⊠ Sym^{r−1} is irreducible on the preimage SL₂ × SL₂, using r − 1 < t. The case M_π ∩ M_σ = F is not discussed separately either; the same argument covers it. The conclusion stands, so this affects nothing. It is a separate defect from E25, which is about irreducibility over F(ζ_t).
findings.evidence: Proof of Lemma 5.7, p. 41: 'If M_π ∩ M_σ ≠ F then either M_π ∩ M_σ/F is quadratic or M_π = M_σ … In the quadratic case the restriction of each of r̄_{π,ι_t} and Sym^{r−1} r̄_{σ,ι_t} to G_{M_π∩M_σ} is irreducible, so the tensor product is irreducible.'

Correction: use linear disjointness of M_π and M_σ over L = M_π ∩ M_σ (which also covers L = F), so the joint image of G_L contains SL₂(F_{t^a}) × SL₂(F_{t^b}) up to conjugacy, on which Std ⊠ Sym^{r−1} is irreducible because r − 1 < t.

findings.claim: The paper defines F(S) as 'unramified outside S' for a set S of finite places, without saying whether ramification at the real places is allowed. Under the common convention that it is not (F(S) totally real), the dihedral-exclusion step fails: the inducing field K may be CM, and then K ⊄ F(S ∪ {v₂}). This affects Prop. 5.4, p. 39 ('hence K ⊂ F(S ∪ {v₂})') and Lemma 5.7(5), p. 42 ('this implies that v₁ splits in the inducing field (since it splits in F(S))'). Lemma 5.3 and Theorem 5.9 work under either reading. The extraction adopts the permissive reading as a convention but records no sourceIssue. A formaliser reading the paper alone could therefore choose the wrong convention.

findings.claim: Lemma 5.8 relies on several facts about Aut(C)-conjugation and coefficient conjugation that no item states. γπ is RAESDC of weight 0 and non-CM (check 1). 'Ordinary of weight 0' is invariant under the action of I_{Q_l}, indeed of G_{Q_l}, on coefficients (check 4). The paper calls the last 'an easy check'.
